title: Social anxiety disorder: SSRI (serotonin reuptake inhibition)
vignette: A 32-year-old man comes to the office due to anxiety that has intensified since he was promoted to a managerial position. Whereas he previously worked alone, his new position requires him to interact with a team of five employees and handle customer service complaints. The patient says he is anxious throughout the day and fears that he will say something embarrassing or that his coworkers and customers will notice his anxiety and think he is incompetent. He says he was very quiet and shy growing up and would always get anxious when meeting new people. He has a few friends with whom he socializes, but he typically has three or four alcoholic drinks before going out with them to feel more relaxed. The patient does not feel depressed, and his sleep and appetite are normal. A medication with which of the following mechanisms of action would be most appropriate for this patient?

clues.text: fears that he will say something embarrassing or that his coworkers and customers will notice his anxiety and think he is incompetent
clues.note: Fear of scrutiny, embarrassment, and negative evaluation in social/performance situations is the core of social anxiety disorder (social phobia).

clues.text: very quiet and shy growing up and would always get anxious when meeting new people
clues.note: A long-standing pattern beginning in childhood/adolescence is typical of social anxiety disorder.

clues.text: three or four alcoholic drinks before going out
clues.note: Self-medication with alcohol to reduce social anxiety is common and a reason to avoid benzodiazepines (dependence risk).

clues.text: does not feel depressed, and his sleep and appetite are normal
clues.note: Absence of depressive symptoms points to a primary anxiety disorder; first-line pharmacotherapy is still an SSRI/SNRI.

whatMatters: Pervasive fear of scrutiny/embarrassment in social situations since childhood = SOCIAL ANXIETY DISORDER. First-line pharmacotherapy is a drug that inhibits SEROTONIN REUPTAKE (an SSRI, or SNRI). Answer F. Because he self-medicates with alcohol, benzodiazepines (GABA agonists) are avoided.
strategy: Diagnose generalized social anxiety disorder, then pick first-line medication = SSRI/SNRI (serotonin reuptake inhibition) + CBT. Reject beta blockers (only for PERFORMANCE-only subtype, as-needed), benzodiazepines (GABA-A agonism; avoid with alcohol misuse), antipsychotics (dopamine/serotonin antagonism; not indicated), antihistamines (H1 antagonism; sedation, not effective), and MAO inhibitors (effective but not first-line: dietary/side-effect issues).

eliminations.label: Beta blockade - performance-only subtype, as needed
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: beta blockers blunt physical symptoms (tachycardia, tremor) for PERFORMANCE-only social anxiety, taken as needed. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has GENERALIZED, daily social anxiety, not isolated performance anxiety, so a daily SSRI is preferred. ✅ Correct if: stage fright/performance-only anxiety.

eliminations.label: Dopamine/serotonin receptor antagonism - antipsychotics
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: second-generation antipsychotic mechanism. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: antipsychotics are not indicated for social anxiety disorder. ✅ Correct if: psychotic or bipolar disorder.

eliminations.label: GABA-A agonism - benzodiazepines (avoid with alcohol misuse)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: benzodiazepines enhance GABA-A activity and are effective for anxiety. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they are second-line due to tolerance/dependence and should be AVOIDED in this patient who self-medicates with alcohol. ✅ Correct if: short-term anxiety without substance-use risk.

eliminations.label: Histamine receptor antagonism - antihistamines (sedation)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: H1 antagonists (e.g., hydroxyzine, diphenhydramine) that cause sedation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they are not effective first-line treatment for social anxiety disorder. ✅ Correct if: mild situational sedation/allergy, not a primary anxiety treatment.

eliminations.label: Monoamine oxidase inhibition - effective but not first-line
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: MAO inhibitors, which do help social anxiety. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they are NOT first-line because of dietary tyramine restrictions and side effects/interactions. ✅ Correct if: refractory social anxiety after SSRIs/SNRIs.

reasoning: Fear of scrutiny/embarrassment in social situations since childhood = social anxiety disorder
First-line pharmacotherapy = SSRI (or SNRI) plus cognitive-behavioral therapy
SSRIs act by inhibiting serotonin reuptake
mechanism: Social anxiety disorder (social phobia) is marked by persistent (>=6 months) marked anxiety about one or more social situations in which the person fears scrutiny, humiliation, or embarrassment; situations are avoided or endured with intense distress, causing functional impairment. Onset is typically in childhood/adolescence, and it is frequently complicated by depression and self-medication with alcohol (as here). First-line pharmacotherapy is a drug that inhibits SEROTONIN REUPTAKE - an SSRI (or an SNRI) - which increases synaptic serotonin availability; cognitive-behavioral therapy is equally first-line. Beta blockers are reserved for the PERFORMANCE-ONLY subtype (as-needed for physical symptoms), and benzodiazepines are second-line and should be avoided in patients with alcohol or other substance misuse because of dependence potential. MAO inhibitors are effective but not first-line owing to dietary tyramine restrictions and drug interactions; antipsychotics and antihistamines are not indicated.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Psych > social anxiety disorder: fear of scrutiny/embarrassment; first-line SSRI/SNRI + CBT; beta blocker/benzodiazepine only for performance-only subtype (benzodiazepine avoided with substance misuse).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Generalized (daily) social anxiety -> first-line SSRI (serotonin reuptake inhibition), not a performance-only beta blocker.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on social anxiety disorder, SSRI/SNRI, performance-only subtype, or GABA-A agonism? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Beta blocker = performance-only; benzodiazepine (GABA) avoided with alcohol misuse; antipsychotic/antihistamine not indicated; MAOI not first-line.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: social anxiety disorder -> SSRI/SNRI + CBT first-line; beta blocker for performance-only; avoid benzodiazepines with substance misuse.
